name: Cui Yu
description: 'Jade'. Developed in 1981 by Taiwan's Tea Research and Extension Station (TRES), Cui Yu was bred for its powerful, unforgettable floral aroma. Often compared to magnolia and lily, it has become a cornerstone of modern Taiwanese oolongs, beloved for its high yield and fragrant character.
plantType: Early-sprouting, high-yielding arbor type (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis)
environment: Thrives in the misty, humid conditions of mid-to-high elevations (400-1,200m). Known for its vigor and good resistance to drought.
processing: Cui Yu's signature floral aroma is best expressed through controlled, light processing that emphasizes its natural aromatics over heavy-roast flavors.
oxidation: Typically undergoes light oxidation (15-30%) for oolongs. The extended withering process is crucial for developing its complex magnolia and gardenia notes.
roasting: Generally unroasted or receives a very light, low-temperature finishing roast for drying purposes. Heavy roasting can easily overwhelm its delicate floral bouquet.
versatility: It is a versatile cultivar. While ideal for light oolongs, careful full oxidation can produce a uniquely aromatic black tea that retains some of its floral heritage.

Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Baozhong: Lightly oxidized, twisted-leaf style that maximizes its fresh floral bouquet.
Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).High-Mountain Oolong: Ball-rolled style from high elevations, creating a thicker, creamier mouthfeel.
Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Dong Ding Oolong (Modern Style): Modern, lightly roasted interpretations that focus on a fresh, floral character.
Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Jade Oolong: A common commercial name for any lightly oxidized Cui Yu oolong.

Black Tea (Aromatic Expression).Jade Black Tea: A smooth black tea with notes of lychee and honey, retaining a floral background.

Experimental & Boutique Styles.White Tea: Creates a delicate tea with soft, sweet notes of hay and wildflowers.
Experimental & Boutique Styles.Green Tea: Rare, yields a brisk, vegetal tea where the floral notes are more subdued.

sensory.aroma: Intense Magnolia, Gardenia, Lily, Fresh Cream
sensory.flavor: Sugarcane, Buttery, Clean vegetal finish, hint of Lychee
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Viscous, smooth, and full-bodied with very low astringency. The liquor is a bright, pale yellow-green to light gold.
